A1.title: Brute-force a weak hash commitment
A1.verdict: Move space is only 3 values, so without a large random salt the commitment hides nothing. A 256-bit salt makes guessing infeasible.

A2.title: Malleability: copycat C′ = C + G
A2.verdict: Without a proof of knowledge the attacker wins 65.5% of rounds (fair play: 33.3%). With the context-bound Okamoto proof, 1000/1000 mauled commitments were rejected at commit time.

A3.title: Copy / replay an opponent's commitment

vulnerable.effect: attacker mirrors the victim and forces a draw every round (or replays an old match)

A3.verdict: Binding the commitment to tournament/match/round/player and signing it with the player's Ed25519 key makes copied or replayed commitments fail verification.

A4.title: Trapdoor generator H = t·G (equivocation)
A4.verdict: Binding only holds if nobody knows log_G(H). CommitRPS derives H with RFC 9380 hash-to-curve from a public string, so the operator has no trapdoor.

A5.title: Weak RNG: blinding factor from 16-bit Math.random()

mitigated.note: r is uniform in Z_ℓ (64 CSPRNG bytes mod ℓ). Pedersen is then perfectly hiding: for every move m′ there exists an r′ with C = m′G + r′H, so even an unbounded attacker learns nothing.

A5.verdict: The commitment is only as hiding as its randomness. A low-entropy r lets the opponent read your move before you reveal it.

A6.title: Timing leak in secret comparison
A6.verdict: An early-exit comparison takes longer the more leading characters match, so an attacker can recover a secret byte by byte. CommitRPS hashes session tokens and compares with crypto.timingSafeEqual / a branch-free loop.

A7.title: Selective abort after seeing the opponent's reveal
A7.verdict: Commitments cannot force someone to open them. Without a deadline, a cheater never loses — matches just stall. CommitRPS enforces a reveal deadline and awards the match to the player who did reveal.

A8.title: Malicious referee swaps a commitment

vulnerable.note: Without signatures, players would have to trust the server's copy of every commitment.

A8.verdict: Every commit and reveal is signed by the player's Ed25519 key, and every browser re-verifies the opponent's signature, proof and opening. The referee can delay, but cannot change a move undetected.
